==English== {{wp}} ===Etymology=== {{root|en|ine-pro|*skey-}} The verb is from {{inh|en|enm|schiften}}, from {{inh|en|ang|sċiftan|t=to divide, separate into shares; appoint, ordain; arrange, organise}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*skiftijan}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*skiftijaną}}, {{m|gem-pro|*skiptijaną}}, from earlier {{m|gem-pro|*skipatjaną|t=to organise, put in order}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*skeyb-|t=to separate, divide, part}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*skey-|t=to cut, divide, separate, part}}. Cognate with {{cog|sco|schift}}, {{m|sco|skift|t=to shift}}, {{cog|fy|skifte}}, {{m|fy|skiftsje|t=to sort}}, {{cog|nl|schiften|t=to sort, screen, winnow, part}}, {{cog|nds|schichten|t=to stack, layer}}, {{cog|de|schichten|t=to stack, layer}}, {{cog|sv|skifta|t=to shift, change, exchange, vary}}, {{cog|no|skifte|t=to shift}}, {{cog|is|skipta|t=to switch}}. See {{m|en|ship}}. The noun is from {{inh|en|enm|schyft}}, {{m|enm|shyffte}}. Cognate with {{cog|nl|schift|t=split, fissure}}, {{cog|de|Schicht|t=layer, shift}}. ===Pronunciation=== * {{IPA|en|/ˈʃɪft/|[ˈʃʰɪft]}} ** {{audio|en|en-ca-shift.oga|a=CA}} ** {{audio|en|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Vealhurl-shift.wav|a=Southern England}} * {{rhymes|en|ɪft|s=1}} * {{hyph|en|shift}} ===Noun=== {{en-noun|~}} # A movement to do something, a beginning. # An act of shifting; a slight [[movement]] or [[change]]. #: {{ux|en|There was a '''shift''' in the political atmosphere.}} #* '''c. 1620-1626''', {{w|Henry Wotton}}, ''letter to Nicholas Pey'' #* {{RQ:en:New York Times|date=November 7, 2012|author=Matt Bai|title=Winning a Second Term, Obama Will Confront Familiar Headwinds| url=http://www.nytimes.com/2012/11/07/us/politics/in-president-obamas-second-term-familiar-challenges.html| passage=The generational '''shift''' Mr. Obama once embodied is, in fact, well under way, but it will not change Washington as quickly — or as harmoniously — as a lot of voters once hoped.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20200603203209/https://www.nytimes.com/2012/11/07/us/politics/in-president-obamas-second-term-familiar-challenges.html}} # {{lb|en|obsolete}} A share, a portion assigned on division. # {{lb|en|historical}} A type of women's undergarment of dress length worn under dresses or skirts, a [[slip]] or [[chemise]]. #: {{ux|en|Just last week she bought a new '''shift''' at the market.}} #* {{RQ:Fielding Tom Jones|book=V|chapter=X|passage=No; without a gown, in a '''shift''' that was somewhat of the coarsest, and none of the cleanest, bedewed likewise with some odoriferous effluvia, the produce of the day's labour, with a pitchfork in her hand, Molly Seagrim approached.}} #* {{quote-book|en|author=w:Charles Johnstone|title=The Reverie; or, A Flight to the Paradise of Fools|url=http://books.google.com.sg/books?id=1mAzAQAAMAAJ&pg=PA202|volume=2|location=Dublin|publisher=Printed by Dillon Chamberlaine|year=1762|page=202|oclc=519072825|passage=At length, one night, when the company by some accident broke up much sooner than ordinary, so that the candles were not half burnt out, she was not able to resist the temptation, but resolved to have them some way or other. Accordingly, as soon as the hurry was over, and the servants, as she thought, all gone to sleep, she stole out of her bed, and went down stairs, naked to her '''shift''' as she was, with a design to steal them {{...}}}} #* {{RQ:Maugham Moon and Sixpence|[[s:The Moon and Sixpence/Chapter XLVII|chapter 47]]||Some wear black '''shifts''' and flesh-coloured stockings; some with curly hair, dyed yellow, are dressed like little girls in short muslin frocks.}} # A simple straight-hanging, loose-fitting dress. #* {{RQ:Gordon Girl in a Band|page=207|chapter=37|text=As part of our antirock stance, Julie and I wore matching housewife-y '''shifts''' and Pro Keds and sweated it out in the ninety-plus-degree heat.}} # A change of workers, now specifically a set group of workers or period of working time. #: {{syn|en|workshift|turn of duty}} #: {{ux|en|We'll work three '''shifts''' a day till the job's done.}} # {{lb|en|US}} The [[gear]] mechanism in a motor vehicle. #: {{ux|en|Does it come with a stick-'''shift'''?}} # {{alt case|en|Shift||a modifier button of computer keyboards}}. #: {{ux|en|If you press '''shift'''-P, the preview display will change.}} # {{lb|en|computing}} A [[control code]] or [[character]] used to change between different [[character set]]s. ## {{lb|en|computing}} An instance of the use of such a code or character. # {{lb|en|computing}} A [[bit shift]]. # {{lb|en|baseball}} An [[infield shift]]. #: {{ux|en|Teams often use a '''shift''' against this lefty.}} # {{lb|en|Ireland|crude|_|slang|often with the definite article|usually|_|uncountable}} The act of kissing passionately. #* {{quote-book|en|year=2023|author=Colin Walsh|title=Kala |passage=She flicked her hair out of her eyes again and looked into yours as you put your hands on her waist. Then her tongue was in your mouth and yours was in hers. You were getting the '''shift'''. Ye were shifting.}} # {{lb|en|archaic}} A [[contrivance]], a [[device]] to try when other methods fail. #* {{RQ:Shakespeare King John|text=If I get down, and do not break my limbs,
I'll find a thousand '''shifts''' to get away:
